DoS.title: Denial of Service (DoS)
DoS.summary: A single source floods a service with requests or holds connections open (e.g. Hulk, GoldenEye, Slowloris, Slowhttptest) so legitimate users cannot be served.
DoS.impact: Service slowdown or outage, exhausted server resources (CPU, memory, connection slots), possible cover for other attacks.
DoS.indicators: Very high packet or request rate from few sources, many long-held or half-open HTTP connections, unusual idle times between packets, traffic concentrated on web ports (80/443).

recommendations.action: Apply rate limiting per source IP at the web server or reverse proxy
recommendations.why: Caps how many requests one client can make, which directly limits a single-source flood.

recommendations.action: Tune connection timeouts and maximum concurrent connections
recommendations.why: Slow attacks (Slowloris, Slowhttptest) work by holding connections open; shorter timeouts free those slots.

recommendations.action: Place the service behind a CDN or Web Application Firewall (WAF)
recommendations.why: These absorb and filter abusive traffic before it reaches your server.

recommendations.action: Temporarily block the offending source after confirming it is malicious
recommendations.why: Stops the current attack; confirm first to avoid blocking legitimate users behind shared IPs.

recommendations.action: Monitor server resources and set alerts for traffic spikes
recommendations.why: Early warning shortens the time to respond to the next attack.

DDoS.title: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)
DDoS.summary: Many sources flood a target at the same time, overwhelming bandwidth or the service itself. Harder to stop than DoS because blocking one source does not help.
DDoS.impact: Full service outage, saturated network links, costs from scaling or bandwidth, business disruption.
DDoS.indicators: Large volume of short flows from many sources toward the same destination, high packet rate, abnormal packet size patterns, sudden traffic surge compared to baseline.

recommendations.action: Enable a DDoS protection service (CDN / cloud scrubbing)
recommendations.why: Distributed floods exceed what a single server can filter; providers absorb traffic across their global network.

recommendations.action: Apply upstream traffic filtering with your ISP or hosting provider
recommendations.why: Filtering before traffic reaches your link prevents bandwidth saturation.

recommendations.action: Use rate limiting and geo / reputation-based filtering at the edge
recommendations.why: Reduces the volume that reaches the application while keeping legitimate traffic flowing.

recommendations.action: Scale infrastructure horizontally (load balancer, autoscaling)
recommendations.why: Buys time and capacity while mitigation is put in place.

recommendations.action: Prepare an incident response plan for availability attacks
recommendations.why: Knowing who to call and what to switch on reduces downtime.

BruteForce.title: Brute-Force Authentication Attack
BruteForce.summary: An automated tool repeatedly tries usernames and passwords against a login service (e.g. FTP or SSH) hoping to guess valid credentials.
BruteForce.impact: Account compromise, unauthorized access to systems and data, use of the compromised account for further attacks.
BruteForce.indicators: Many short, similar connections from the same source to an authentication port (21 FTP, 22 SSH), consistent packet sizes, high connection rate. Flow data cannot see whether a login succeeded; that must be confirmed in authentication logs.

recommendations.action: Review authentication logs for the targeted service
recommendations.why: Network flows show the pattern but not login success; logs confirm whether any account was accessed.

recommendations.action: Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA)
recommendations.why: A guessed password alone is then not enough to log in.

recommendations.action: Add account lockout or login rate limiting (e.g. fail2ban)
recommendations.why: Slows automated guessing to the point where it becomes impractical.

recommendations.action: Use key-based SSH authentication and disable password login
recommendations.why: Removes the password attack surface for SSH entirely.

recommendations.action: Enforce a strong password policy and check for reused passwords
recommendations.why: Guessing tools rely on common and leaked passwords.

recommendations.action: Block the source IP after confirming malicious activity
recommendations.why: Stops the current attempt; attackers may rotate IPs, so combine with the measures above.

PortScan.title: Port / Network Scanning
PortScan.summary: A source probes many ports or hosts to discover which services are running. Scanning is usually reconnaissance before an actual attack.
PortScan.impact: Exposure of running services and versions to an attacker, often followed by exploitation attempts against what was found.
PortScan.indicators: Many very short flows from one source across many destination ports, few packets per flow, little or no payload data, connections that end right after the handshake.

recommendations.action: Review firewall rules and allow only required ports
recommendations.why: Every unnecessary open port is something a scanner can find and attack.

recommendations.action: Close or disable services that are not needed
recommendations.why: Reduces the attack surface discovered by the scan.

recommendations.action: Segment the network so internal services are not reachable from outside
recommendations.why: Limits what a scanner can reach even if it gets a foothold.

recommendations.action: Monitor the scanning source for follow-up activity
recommendations.why: Scans often precede exploitation; watching the source gives early warning.

recommendations.action: Patch the services that are exposed
recommendations.why: Attackers will look for known vulnerabilities in the versions they discovered.

Anomaly.title: Anomalous Traffic
Anomaly.summary: Traffic that the anomaly detector (Isolation Forest trained only on normal traffic) considers unusual, but that does not match a known attack class. It may be a new attack, misconfiguration, or simply rare but legitimate behavior.
Anomaly.impact: Unknown. Needs investigation before conclusions are drawn.
Anomaly.indicators: Flow statistics far from the normal-traffic baseline. The detector is calibrated to flag about 1% of normal traffic, so it is only reported as an incident when the anomaly rate is clearly above that noise level.

recommendations.action: Investigate the source and destination of the unusual flows
recommendations.why: Identifying who is talking to what is the first step to deciding if this is benign.

recommendations.action: Compare against the normal baseline and recent changes
recommendations.why: New software, backups or deployments often explain unusual traffic.

recommendations.action: Review related system and application logs
recommendations.why: Logs give context that flow statistics alone cannot provide.

recommendations.action: Keep monitoring the activity over time
recommendations.why: A one-off may be noise; a persistent pattern deserves escalation.

Phishing.title: Phishing URL
Phishing.summary: A link designed to trick users into entering credentials or personal data on a fake page that imitates a trusted brand.
Phishing.impact: Stolen credentials, account takeover, financial fraud, further compromise of the organization.
Phishing.indicators: Login / verify / account keywords, look-alike domains, many subdomains, raw IP addresses, '@' symbols, URL shorteners, long obfuscated URLs.

recommendations.action: Do not enter credentials or personal data on the page
recommendations.why: The page's purpose is to capture what you type.

recommendations.action: Navigate to the real site by typing its address yourself
recommendations.why: Avoids look-alike domains entirely.

recommendations.action: Report the link to your security team or email provider
recommendations.why: Helps block it for other users.

recommendations.action: If credentials were entered, change the password immediately and enable MFA
recommendations.why: Limits how long a stolen password stays useful.

Malware.title: Malware Distribution URL
Malware.summary: A link that delivers malicious software, either as a direct download or by exploiting the browser when the page is visited.
Malware.impact: Infection of the device, data theft, ransomware, use of the device in further attacks.
Malware.indicators: Direct links to executables or archives (.exe, .zip, .apk), raw IP hosts, unusual paths, obfuscated parameters.

recommendations.action: Do not download or open files from the link
recommendations.why: Execution of the file is usually the infection step.

recommendations.action: Run an antivirus scan if anything was downloaded
recommendations.why: Detects and removes known malware early.

recommendations.action: Keep the browser and operating system updated
recommendations.why: Drive-by attacks exploit known, already patched vulnerabilities.

recommendations.action: Block the domain at DNS or firewall level for your network
recommendations.why: Protects other users from the same link.

Defacement.title: Defaced / Compromised Website URL
Defacement.summary: The URL pattern resembles pages of websites that have been compromised and altered by attackers, often through vulnerable CMS components.
Defacement.impact: The site may host attacker content or malicious scripts; trust in the site is reduced.
Defacement.indicators: CMS-style query strings (e.g. index.php?option=com_...), many parameters, patterns typical of vulnerable plugins.

recommendations.action: Avoid interacting with the page or entering any data
recommendations.why: Compromised sites can serve malicious scripts.

recommendations.action: If you own the site: patch the CMS, plugins and themes
recommendations.why: Defacement usually exploits outdated components.

recommendations.action: If you own the site: restore from a clean backup and rotate admin credentials
recommendations.why: Removes attacker changes and any access they kept.

recommendations.action: Deploy a WAF and enable file integrity monitoring
recommendations.why: Detects and blocks future tampering.
